To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spatial proximity to CAFs impacts molecular features, therapeutic sensitivity, and clinical outcomes of breast cancer cells.

(1) Cancer-associated fibroblastic (CAF) cells induce subtype-specific changes in the expression of genes and metabolic pathways of carcinoma cells in a 3D coculture model, (2) these CAF-induced changes are associated with clinical outcome, and (3) CAFs protect HER2+ breast carcinoma cells from the HER2-targeting drug lapatinib, but this protective effect is reversible by inhibiting JAK2 or the hyaluronic-acid receptor CD44
cancer-associated fibroblast-induced molecular features in breast cancer cells impact clinical outcomes and can be targeted for therapeutic benefit.

the role of the microenvironment, in particular cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF), in breast cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of breast cancer progression and metastasis and the identification of new therapeutic targets.
the impact of the tumor microenvironment, particularly cancer-associated fibroblast cells (CAFs), on breast cancer cells and their responses to targeted therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CAFs can alter gene expression profiles of breast cancer and that this can have a significant impact on clinical outcome.

the proximity of breast cancer cells to CAF in the tumor microenvironment has a significant impact on the molecular features of breast cancer cells, including the sensitivity to lapatinib, and thus on the clinical outcome of breast cancer patients.
the authors demonstrate that CAFs have a strong impact on cancer cells, and this can be utilized in a variety of ways to improve treatment of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-induced changes in the molecular features of carcinoma cells impact therapeutic sensitivity and patient clinical outcomes.
cancer cells are influenced by their microenvironment and that this influence has clinical consequences.
the microenvironment is a key determinant of the biology of breast cancers and that it is critical to consider this when developing and implementing new therapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer cells are not just floating in a liquid environment.

breast cancer cells in close proximity to cancer-associated fibroblast are protected from HER2 inhibitors, and that the inhibition of JAK2/ STAT3 and/or the inhibition of hyaluronan metabolism sensitizes breast cancer cells to HER2 inhibitors.

the tumor microenvironment, which is composed of cancer cells, immune cells and stromal cells, has an impact on how the cancer cells behave, and this has implications on the efficacy of the cancer therapies.
